findings.location: Proof 2.1, the rational enumeration and termination argument for choosing x₀ in (-1,1) outside the root set
findings.evidence: The proof asserts that enumerating reduced rationals in (-1,1) and choosing the first point outside the finite root set terminates because the nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots. Finiteness of the root set alone does not establish that the rational candidates are infinite or dense in (-1,1), or that the enumeration covers them. The cited dependencies def-real-numbers, thm-reals-field, and thm-reals-ordered-field give the real construction and field/order structure, but no density, infinitude, or enumeration result for the rationals. A short proof of rational density/infinitude in the interval or an authoritative source is needed. This is a nonfatal omission because the elementary density argument closes it immediately.
